title: Design a notification service
summary: Push, email and SMS for 20 M users: priority queues, preferences and quiet hours, a dedupe window, per-user caps, provider failover and retries that never send twice.

steps.title: Requirements and estimates
body: **The ask:** one service every team calls to tell users things: "your order shipped", "your login code is 4821",
"this week's digest". It picks the channel, respects the user's settings and talks to the providers.
| Kind | Requirement |
| Functional | send to a user by event type; channels: mobile push, email, SMS; preferences and quiet hours; templates per language |
| Non-functional | one-time codes delivered within seconds; marketing can wait; **never send the same notification twice**; survive a provider outage |
| Out of scope | the marketing campaign editor, in-app inbox UI |
```text
users          20 M
normal load    5 notifications / user / day = 100 M / day   ≈ 1,200 / s average
campaigns      a 10 M email campaign sent over 1 hour     ≈ 2,800 / s on top
providers      each has its own rate limit and its own outages
The design problem is not volume: it is **mixing urgent and bulk traffic**, and **retrying safely** through
providers you do not control.

steps.prompt: A campaign of 30 M emails must finish within 2 hours. What send rate must the email path sustain, on top of normal traffic?
steps.explain: 30,000,000 / 7,200 s ≈ 4,167 per second. If one provider account accepts 2,000 per second you need three accounts or two providers, and the campaign must not starve the one-time codes.

steps.title: The pipeline
body: ```text
callers --> POST /notify --> validate, look up user + preferences
v                                     v
[ high-priority queue ]               [ bulk queue ]
codes, security alerts                digests, marketing
channel workers (push / email / SMS), each with its own rate limit
APNs, FCM      email provider A      SMS provider A
email provider B      SMS provider B   (failover)
delivery log: (notification_id, channel, status, provider, attempts)
- **Separate queues and workers per priority.** A bulk campaign then cannot sit in front of a login code.
- **Workers own the provider limits** (push services, email and SMS providers all throttle). Back off on their
`429`s instead of hammering them.
- The **delivery log** is the source of truth for "was this sent?" and the analytics behind it.

steps.prompt: Which queue should each notification go to?
items: "3 people viewed your profile this week"
steps.explain: Anything a user is actively waiting for, or that protects their account, is high priority. Everything else can wait minutes or hours and should be throttled so it never delays the first group.

steps.title: Dedupe, quiet hours and caps
body: - **Idempotency key.** Every request carries a key (`order-81723:shipped`). The service records it; the same key
again within the **dedupe window** is dropped. Callers retry; users should not notice.
- **Pass the key to the provider too.** If a provider call times out you do not know whether it was sent. Retry
with the same key where the provider supports one, and record the outcome before acking the queue message.
- **Quiet hours** are in the user's own time zone and wrap past midnight (22:00 to 07:00). Non-urgent messages
are **deferred**, not dropped. Security messages bypass them.
- **Per-user caps** (say 3 marketing pushes a day) stop teams from spamming the same user from different
services: this service is the one place that sees all of them.

steps.prompt: Quiet hours can wrap past midnight. What does this print?
code: bool Quiet(int hour, int start, int end) =>
start > end ? hour >= start || hour < end : hour >= start && hour < end;
steps.explain: When start > end the window wraps: quiet if the hour is late (>= 22) or early (< 7). 07:00 itself is the end, so it is no longer quiet. Without the wrap case, a 22-to-7 window would never match.

prompt: **Symptom first.** After a 20-minute slowdown at the push provider, support gets complaints: some users received
the same "Your order shipped" push three times. The worker log:
```text
12:01:07 notif=8812 push attempt=1 timeout after 10s -> requeue
12:01:19 notif=8812 push attempt=2 timeout after 10s -> requeue
12:01:33 notif=8812 push attempt=3 status=200
What is the most likely cause?
options: The timed-out attempts had actually been delivered. Timeouts were retried as failures with no idempotency key or dedupe check before resending
The provider has a bug that duplicates pushes
Three workers consumed the same queue message at once
steps.explain: A timeout means "unknown", not "failed". The fix: record attempts in the delivery log, pass an idempotency key to the provider where it supports one, collapse duplicates on the device (a collapse key), and check the dedupe window before every resend.

steps.prompt: Put one worker's steps for a notification in order.
lines: Take the next message from the priority queue
Drop it if the same idempotency key was sent within the dedupe window
Check the user's preferences and quiet hours for this channel
Render the template in the user's language
Call the provider with the idempotency key and record the result in the delivery log
Ack the queue message only after the result is recorded
also: Take the next message from the priority queue
Check the user's preferences and quiet hours for this channel
Drop it if the same idempotency key was sent within the dedupe window
Render the template in the user's language
Call the provider with the idempotency key and record the result in the delivery log
Ack the queue message only after the result is recorded
steps.explain: Acking last gives at-least-once processing: a crash before the ack redelivers the message, and the dedupe check makes that safe.

steps.title: Provider failover
prompt: Write `string PickProvider(string[] providers, Dictionary<string, double> errorRate, double maxError)`:
- `providers` are in order of preference.
- Return the first one whose recent error rate is at most `maxError`. A provider missing from `errorRate` has no
recent errors (rate `0`).
- If none qualifies, return `"none"` (the worker then parks the message and alerts).
starter: string PickProvider(string[] providers, Dictionary<string, double> errorRate, double maxError)
solution: string PickProvider(string[] providers, Dictionary<string, double> errorRate, double maxError)
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoP = new[] { "mail-a", "mail-b" };
Dojo.Eq("the preferred provider when it is healthy", "mail-a", PickProvider(dojoP, new Dictionary<string, double> { ["mail-a"] = 0.01 }, 0.05));
Dojo.Eq("fail over when it is not", "mail-b", PickProvider(dojoP, new Dictionary<string, double> { ["mail-a"] = 0.4, ["mail-b"] = 0.02 }, 0.05));
Dojo.Eq("no data means healthy", "mail-a", PickProvider(dojoP, new Dictionary<string, double>(), 0.05));
Dojo.Eq("exactly at the limit is fine", "mail-a", PickProvider(dojoP, new Dictionary<string, double> { ["mail-a"] = 0.05 }, 0.05));
Dojo.Eq("everything is failing", "none", PickProvider(dojoP, new Dictionary<string, double> { ["mail-a"] = 0.9, ["mail-b"] = 0.7 }, 0.05));

steps.title: Dedupe and quiet hours
prompt: Write a class `Notifier` that decides what to do with each notification. Time is in whole minutes since a
midnight in the user's time zone (`nowMinute`), so the hour of the day is `nowMinute % 1440 / 60`.
- `Notifier(int dedupeWindowMinutes, int quietStartHour, int quietEndHour)`: hours outside 0-23 throw
`ArgumentOutOfRangeException`. The quiet window may wrap past midnight; start equal to end means no quiet hours.
- `string Decide(string user, string key, bool critical, long nowMinute)`, checked in this order:
1. `"dup"` if this user got this key **sent** less than `dedupeWindowMinutes` ago.
2. `"defer"` if it is not critical and the hour is in quiet hours (nothing is recorded: it will come back).
3. Otherwise `"send"`, and remember the time it was sent for this user and key.
starter: public Notifier(int dedupeWindowMinutes, int quietStartHour, int quietEndHour) { }
public string Decide(string user, string key, bool critical, long nowMinute) => "send";
solution: readonly Dictionary<(string User, string Key), long> sent = new();
public Notifier(int dedupeWindowMinutes, int quietStartHour, int quietEndHour)
return start > end ? hour >= start || hour < end : hour >= start && hour < end;
public string Decide(string user, string key, bool critical, long nowMinute)
if (sent.TryGetValue((user, key), out var at) && nowMinute - at < window) return "dup";
hints: Remember sends in a `Dictionary<(string User, string Key), long>`.
The quiet check is the one from the predict step, with `hour = (int)(nowMinute % 1440 / 60)`.
template: var dojoN = new Notifier(60, 22, 7);
Dojo.Eq("10:00, first time: send", "send", dojoN.Decide("ana", "like:42", false, 600));
Dojo.Eq("30 minutes later: duplicate", "dup", dojoN.Decide("ana", "like:42", false, 630));
Dojo.Eq("another user is not a duplicate", "send", dojoN.Decide("bo", "like:42", false, 630));
Dojo.Eq("60 minutes later the window has passed", "send", dojoN.Decide("ana", "like:42", false, 660));
Dojo.Eq("23:00, not critical: defer", "defer", dojoN.Decide("ana", "digest", false, 1380));
Dojo.Eq("23:00, critical: send", "send", dojoN.Decide("ana", "otp:9", true, 1380));
Dojo.Eq("critical repeats are still deduped", "dup", dojoN.Decide("ana", "otp:9", true, 1390));
Dojo.Eq("06:40 next day: still quiet", "defer", dojoN.Decide("ana", "digest", false, 1440 + 400));
Dojo.Eq("07:00 next day: send the deferred digest", "send", dojoN.Decide("ana", "digest", false, 1440 + 420));
var dojoDay = new Notifier(10, 9, 17);
Dojo.Eq("a daytime quiet window (no wrap)", "defer", dojoDay.Decide("cy", "x", false, 600));
Dojo.Eq("after it ends", "send", dojoDay.Decide("cy", "x", false, 17 * 60));
var dojoNone = new Notifier(10, 0, 0);
Dojo.Eq("start equal to end: never quiet", "send", dojoNone.Decide("dee", "x", false, 120));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentOutOfRangeException>("hour 24 is invalid", () => new Notifier(10, 24, 7));
